evidence.quote: Consider $n$ positive real numbers $\lambda$, and consider the set of all $n \times n$ orthonormal matrices $S$. Prove a tightness bound(s) between the (1) trace error of the optimal column subset selection of the worst case matrix $K$ possessing eigenvalues $\lambda$: \begin{equation} x_k (\lambda) := \max_{V \in S} \min_{\I \subset [n], |\I| = k} \Tr{K - K_{:,\I} K_{\I, \I}^{-1} K_{\I,:} \biggr\rvert_{K=V^\top \mathrm{diag}(\lambda) V}} \end{equation} and (2) the objective yielded by volume sampling any such $K$: \begin{equation} y_k (\lambda) := \left(\mathbb{E}_{\I \sim k-\mathrm{DPP}(K)} \Tr{K- K_{:,\I} K_{\I, \I}^{-1} K_{\I, :}}\right) \bigr\rvert_{K=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda)} = (k+1) \frac{e_{k+1} (\lambda)}{e_k(\lambda)} \end{equation} which is dependent on $\lambda$ alone in terms of the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_k$\cite{Guruswami2012-optimal}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 1$ be an integer, fix $k \in \{1,\dots,n-1\}$, and let $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ be a vector of positive real numbers. Let $S$ denote the set of $n \times n$ real orthogonal matrices. For a positive semidefinite matrix $K \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and a subset $\mathcal{I} \subseteq [n] := \{1,\dots,n\}$, write $K_{:,\mathcal{I}}$ for the submatrix of $K$ formed by the columns indexed by $\mathcal{I}$, $K_{\mathcal{I},:}$ for the submatrix of rows indexed by $\mathcal{I}$, and $K_{\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I}}$ for the principal submatrix indexed by $\mathcal{I}$. Define the worst-case optimal $k$-column subset trace error among matrices with spectrum $\lambda$ by
$$x_k(\lambda) := \max_{V \in S}\; \min_{\substack{\mathcal{I} \subseteq [n] \\ |\mathcal{I}|=k}} \operatorname{Tr}\!\left( K - K_{:,\mathcal{I}} K_{\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I}}^{-1} K_{\mathcal{I},:} \right) \Bigg|_{K = V^\top \operatorname{diag}(\lambda) V}.$$
A $k$-DPP with kernel $K$ is the probability distribution on size-$k$ subsets $\mathcal{I} \subseteq [n]$ given by $\Pr(\mathcal{I}) \propto \det(K_{\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I}})$. Define the volume sampling objective on the diagonal representative by
$$y_k(\lambda) := \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{I} \sim k\text{-DPP}(K)} \operatorname{Tr}\!\left( K - K_{:,\mathcal{I}} K_{\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I}}^{-1} K_{\mathcal{I},:} \right) \Bigg|_{K = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda)} = (k+1)\, \frac{e_{k+1}(\lambda)}{e_k(\lambda)},$$
where $e_j(\lambda)$ denotes the $j$-th elementary symmetric polynomial in $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$.

Establish tight comparison bounds between $x_k(\lambda)$ and $y_k(\lambda)$. Specifically, determine the best (smallest) constants $C_k = C_k(n)$ and $c_k = c_k(n)$, possibly depending on $n$ and $k$ but independent of $\lambda$, such that
$$c_k \cdot y_k(\lambda) \le x_k(\lambda) \le C_k \cdot y_k(\lambda)$$
holds for every vector $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}^n$, and exhibit extremal spectra achieving equality.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific result establishing tight bounds between the worst-case optimal column-subset-selection trace error $x_k(\lambda)$ and the volume-sampling objective $y_k(\lambda) = (k+1) e_{k+1}(\lambda)/e_k(\lambda)$ in the form requested could be located. Standard references (Guruswami–Sinop, Deshpande–Rademacher, Derezinski–Warmuth) provide one-sided bounds via volume sampling but not a matching tightness characterization, so the status is taken to be unknown.
